explanation: A well-formed model uses proper notation, names every entity, provides identifiers, and records relationships clearly. The other choices emphasize implementation shortcuts, temporary labels, or process design rather than model quality.

options.text: Every entity is named, each has an identifier, and the relationships are shown clearly.
The diagram includes only the tables that will likely be cheapest to implement.
Each entity is given a temporary code name so the model can be finalized later.
The model focuses on screen flows because that helps users understand the design.

prompt: A team sketches an ER diagram for a subscription service. Which choice best makes the model well-formed?
